title: JEE Main 2027: NRI Candidates Without Aadhaar Can Now Apply Using Passport
excerpt: The NTA has added a separate 'Apply through the NRI (Having No Aadhaar)' option for Session 1, with applications closing November 22, 2026, at 11:50 p.m. IST.
body:
• NRI candidates who have no Aadhaar card but hold a valid Indian passport can complete the JEE Main 2027 Session 1 application through a separate option on the registration page: "Apply through the NRI (Having No Aadhaar)".
  • Session 1 applications close November 22, 2026, at 11:50 p.m. IST; registration with a late fee runs November 23 to 26, also to 11:50 p.m., according to Careers360's report of the NTA notice.
  • Names, parents' names and date of birth on the form must match the passport and the Class 10 board certificate exactly, Jagran Josh reports.
  • Help from NTA: 011-40759000 or 1800-180-4747, or jeemain@nta.ac.in; apply only on the official portal, jeemain.nta.nic.in.

The National Testing Agency (NTA) has opened a separate application route for Non-Resident Indian candidates applying for JEE Main 2027 Session 1 who do not hold an Aadhaar card. Under the update, an NRI candidate with a valid Indian passport can complete the application through a designated registration option instead of the standard Aadhaar-based route, according to Careers360's report of the NTA notice and Jagran Josh.

Who this affects, exactly

The facility is narrow. Careers360 reports it is only for NRI candidates who do not possess an Aadhaar card but do have a valid Indian passport. Candidates who hold Aadhaar are not affected and use the regular registration route. The clarification followed difficulties overseas applicants reported during the online authentication and e-KYC stages, which run through domestic verification systems such as DigiLocker, JanParichay and e-Pramaan, Jagran Josh reports. Responding to a student query about those authentication barriers, the agency stated, "You can use a passport to complete the application process."

What changed in the application process

Instead of authenticating through the domestic identity systems, an eligible NRI candidate selects the passport route at registration and enters passport details directly into the designated identification fields on the website. The steps, per Careers360, are: visit the official website, jeemain.nta.nic.in; open the JEE Main 2027 Session 1 registration link; on the registration page, select "Apply through the NRI (Having No Aadhaar)"; and continue the application using a valid Indian passport, checking all entered information before submitting.

The details have to line up exactly. Jagran Josh reports that candidates should check the name, parents' names and date of birth entered in the form, and that all details must match their passport records and Class 10 board certificate exactly. The NTA has also advised candidates to refer to its circulars of October 28 and October 30, 2026, regarding alternative login paths and re-KYC workflows.

Dates that matter

The Session 1 registration window is already open and time is short. Candidates can apply until November 22, 2026, up to 11:50 p.m. IST, and can register with a late fee between November 23 and 26, up to 11:50 p.m., according to Careers360. Candidates who previously generated an incomplete application without proper verification have two routes, Jagran Josh reports: apply fresh before the deadline, or use the correction window from November 27 to 29, 2026, to change their identification parameters.

What to do next

Eligible families should apply on the official portal, jeemain.nta.nic.in, and nowhere else, and should keep the candidate's passport and Class 10 certificate side by side while filling the form so every field matches both documents. For help with registration without Aadhaar, candidates can contact the NTA at 011-40759000 or 1800-180-4747, or write to jeemain@nta.ac.in. Official updates are shared on jeemain.nta.nic.in and nta.ac.in, per Careers360.

For an NRI family, the practical risk this notice removes is a stalled application: a student abroad without Aadhaar no longer has to resolve a domestic e-KYC problem before the November 22 deadline. The deadline itself has not moved, so the passport route should be used now, not in the late-fee window.
